Maybe the target molecule is the product SMILES from the mapped_rxn? The mapped_rxn shows product SMILES after >>. That product SMILES is: [CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1

We need to apply template to that product to get precursors. So we should use apply_template with molecule_smiles = that product SMILES (without atom mapping). Remove the mapping tags. The SMILES without mapping: CH3CH2O C(=O)CH2C@H1CH2C@H(O)C@@H(CH3)C@@H(/CH=C(/CH3)C(=O)OCH3)O1? Actually need to convert. Let's just take the product SMILES from mapped_rxn after >>, but remove the atom map numbers and brackets. The string: "[CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3][C:4](=[O:5])[CH2:6][C@H:7]1[CH2:8][C@H:9]([OH:10])[C@@H:11]([CH3:12])[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20])[O:21]1"

We need to strip the brackets and colon numbers. So each atom like [CH3:1] becomes CH3. [C@H:7] becomes C@H. Also need to keep stereochemistry. So final SMILES: "CCO C(=O)CH2C@H1CH2C@H(O)C@@H(CH3)C@@H(/CH=C(/CH3)C(=O)OCH3)O1"? Let's construct:

Start: [CH3:1][CH2:2][O:3] => CH3CH2O (i.e., CCO)
Then [C:4](=[O:5]) => C(=O)
Then [CH2:6] => CH2
Then [C@H:7]1 => C@H1 (start ring)
[CH2:8] => CH2
[C@H:9]([OH:10]) => C@H(O)
[C@@H:11]([CH3:12]) => C@@H(CH3)
[C@@H:13](/[CH:14]=[C:15](/[CH3:16])[C:17](=[O:18])[O:19][CH3:20]) => C@@H(/CH=C(/CH3)C(=O)OCH3)
[O:21]1 => O1 closing ring.

So overall SMILES: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC(O)C(C)C@@H(/CH=C(/CH3)C(=O)OCH3)O1"? Need correct stereochemistry: C@H1 then CH2 then C@H(O) then C@@H(CH3) then C@@H(...). Let's write: "CCOC(=O)C[C@H]1CC(O)C(C)C@@H(/CH=C(/CH3)C(=O)OCH3)O1". But there is also a CH2 after carbonyl: C(=O)CH2. So "CCOC(=O)C" is ethoxy carbonyl? Actually CCOC(=O)C is ethoxy carbonyl attached to CH? The original product likely is a protected sugar derivative with a side chain. Anyway, we can feed the SMILES with mapping removed to apply_template.
